result.rationale: The diff changes the fallback from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the exact case the fallback is meant for), the predicate compares against a falsy value, so `find` returns undefined and the fallback yields undefined where the old code returned the destination calendar's externalId. This occurs identically in both updateEvent and deleteEvent in the Google CalendarService, losing the prior fallback behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent`, the fallback branch was changed from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined, the predicate becomes `cal.externalId === undefined`, which will usually match nothing, so `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` and the prior fallback to the event’s destination calendar is effectively lost. The same pattern exists in `deleteEvent` where `calendarId` is derived via the same `find(...externalCalendarId...)` expression, so the intended fallback to a destination calendar externalId no longer works when `externalCalendarId` isn’t provided.
